27 To produce a stationary wave, two waves must travel in opposite directions through the same
space.
Which statement about the properties of the two waves must also be correct?
A
The waves must have equal frequencies, but different speeds and wavelengths.
B
The waves must have equal speeds, but different wavelengths and frequencies.
C
The waves must have equal speeds, frequencies and wavelengths.
D
The waves must have equal wavelengths, but different speeds and frequencies.

hints: Notice the word must - a stationary wave has nodes that stay in exactly the same position over time.
Recall $v = f\lambda$ for waves in the same space and medium, so speed, frequency and wavelength are linked and cannot be chosen independently.
Ask what happens to the overlap of crests and troughs if the two opposite waves had different $f$ or $\lambda$ - would cancellation stay in the same place?
walkthrough: Identify the given situation: two waves travel in opposite directions through the same space and their superposition must give fixed nodes and antinodes.
State the rule for a stationary wave: the two superposing progressive waves must be of the same type travelling in the same medium, so the magnitude of the wave speed $v$ is the same for both.
For nodes to remain fixed, a point of cancellation must remain cancellation. That requires the two waves to arrive in step cycle after cycle, so the frequency $f$ and wavelength $\lambda$ must match.

Check with $v = f\lambda$: with the same $v$, equal $f$ forces equal $\lambda$, and vice versa. Any difference in $f$ or $\lambda$ makes the phase difference at a point change with time, so the pattern moves.
Therefore speed, frequency and wavelength must all be equal for the two waves. This is option C.

A.explanation: Equal frequencies with different speeds would give different wavelengths from $v = f\lambda$, so the interference pattern would drift and nodes would not stay fixed.

B.explanation: If wavelength and frequency differed, the two waves could not repeatedly superpose in step to keep nodes and antinodes in the same places.

C.explanation: Identical speed, frequency and wavelength in opposite directions gives a stable superposition with fixed nodes and antinodes.

D.explanation: Equal wavelength with different speeds would require different frequencies from $v = f\lambda$, so the phase relationship would change with time and no stationary wave forms.
